templates.name: Static Site Build Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that the build process successfully ingests Markdown notes from an input directory and produces a complete static site output directory with all expected files (HTML, CSS, JS, assets) without errors.

templates.name: Markdown Rendering Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that all Markdown files in the input set (excluding configured ignores) are converted to accessible HTML pages preserving formatting and structure per the supported Markdown flavor.

templates.name: Full-Text Search Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that the search feature returns relevant results matching note titles and body text for representative queries, and that search interaction remains responsive at the confirmed target scale.

templates.name: Tag Browsing and Filtering Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that tag index pages are generated correctly, that selecting a tag displays all notes containing that tag, and that each note page displays its associated tags parsed from the agreed convention.

templates.name: Internal Links and Backlinks Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that internal links between notes render correctly, that each destination note page includes a backlinks section listing all source notes linking to it, and that backlinks are clickable and functional.

templates.name: Static Hosting Compatibility Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that the generated site output can be deployed and served on the target static hosting environment (e.g., local file browsing, GitHub Pages, Netlify) without requiring server-side runtime, and that all pages and features function correctly.

templates.name: Browser Compatibility Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that the generated site loads and functions without errors in modern browsers (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) covering the expected user base.

templates.name: Markdown Flavor Support Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that the supported Markdown features (e.g., CommonMark/GFM, tables, code highlighting, etc.) render correctly in the generated site per the agreed scope.

templates.name: Broken Link Handling Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that broken internal links are detected and handled per the agreed policy (warn, fail build, or render as plain text) and that the behavior is consistent and documented.

templates.name: Build Workflow Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that the build can be invoked via the agreed interface (CLI, GUI, or build script) and that the workflow is documented and repeatable.

coverage_guidance: Ensure test coverage for the full build pipeline from input directory to output directory, including error cases (missing files, malformed Markdown, invalid links).
Test search functionality with a representative corpus at the confirmed scale, including edge cases (empty queries, special characters, very long queries, no results).
Verify tag parsing and normalization across all agreed conventions (YAML front matter, inline hashtags, etc.), including edge cases (empty tags, special characters, case sensitivity, duplicates).

Test internal link resolution for all supported conventions (standard Markdown links, wiki-links, relative paths, etc.), including cross-directory links and edge cases (self-links, circular links, links to non-existent notes).
Verify backlink generation for all valid internal links, including notes with no backlinks and notes with many backlinks.
Test the generated site on the target hosting environment(s) with realistic deployment scenarios (base URL configuration, relative paths, CORS if applicable).
Test browser compatibility on the agreed set of browsers and versions, covering all interactive features (search, navigation, tag filtering).
Verify that the output is fully static (no server-side dependencies) by serving from a simple HTTP server or file system.
Test incremental builds and watch mode (if implemented) to ensure correctness and performance.
Verify that the site information architecture (home, all notes, tags index, per-tag pages, per-note layout) matches the agreed design per Q4.
Test handling of large note sets and edge cases (very large notes, many tags, deeply nested links) to confirm performance targets per Q3.
Verify that the build fails gracefully or warns appropriately for unsupported Markdown features or invalid input per Q6.
definition_of_done: All acceptance test templates have been executed with passing results for the agreed scope and confirmed assumptions.
Build process completes successfully on the target environment(s) without errors for a representative input corpus.
All Markdown notes in the input set are rendered as accessible HTML pages in the output (excluding configured ignores).
Full-text search returns relevant results and performs responsively at the confirmed target scale.
Tag index and per-tag pages are generated correctly, and all notes display their associated tags.
Internal links resolve correctly, and backlinks are generated and displayed on all linked notes.
Generated site can be deployed and functions correctly on the target static hosting environment(s) without server-side runtime.
Site loads and functions without errors in all agreed modern browsers.
All supported Markdown features render correctly per the agreed flavor and scope.
Broken link handling behavior matches the agreed policy and is documented.
Build workflow is documented and repeatable via the agreed interface (CLI, GUI, or build script).
All blocking open questions (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q10) have been resolved and incorporated into the implementation and tests.
Performance, scale, and usability targets per success metrics are met.
Code and build artifacts are delivered with documentation covering usage, supported conventions, and limitations.
